method: After freezing and replaying the decision and canonical record, reread Appendix F and the undergraduate elective and project rules, checked the published specialist course preparation and rebuilt the 180 EC allocation. Reconsidered the primary Earth-system, mathematical, energy and observational course content against the exact finished plan and the threshold for separate physics or astronomy options. This is a separately identified same-AI pass.
findings: Appendix F confirms the 180 EC single-major Physics and Astronomy bachelor for 2026–2027. Teaching is Dutch in year 1, mainly Dutch in year 2 and predominantly English in year 3. The 135 EC major includes 75 EC of taught compulsory courses and the 15 EC supervised project. Its 45 EC elective space includes one 7.5 EC required choice at level 2 and 37.5 EC of major electives including at least 30 EC at level 3. The remaining 45 EC is profiling. Climate, experimental and theoretical physics are study-advice paths, not compulsory degree routes.

The first-year rules include six taught compulsory courses, one profiling course and one major elective. Atmosphere and Ocean Dynamics is a first-year eligible elective, offered in period 3, with mechanics and calculus preparation. The earlier example fixed level-3 courses without proving timetable and preparation compatibility. The corrected comparison gives the actual four-course choice and illustrates geophysical fluid dynamics and turbulence without assigning them to semesters. Fluid Mechanics and Transport Phenomena calls for Mathematical Techniques 1–3. Advanced Quantum Mechanics builds on Quantum Mechanics and Mathematical Techniques 1–3. Geophysical Fluid Dynamics builds on wave dynamics and continuum or fluid mechanics, while Turbulence in Fluids calls for fluid mechanics and thermodynamics. The final research project normally requires the compulsory taught courses and at least 90 EC, a supervised project agreed before the semester and signed paperwork; exceptions require approval. It culminates in a written thesis and oral presentation.

The plan directly supports climate and Earth-system questions through Earth System Science Tools (modeling, proxies and isotope tracers), Climate Change (forcing, feedbacks and consequences), Earth Observation (remote sensing, spectral signatures and spatial analysis), and environmental biogeochemistry (aqueous and mineral reactions and carbon cycling). Dynamic Earth and hazards support physical Earth processes; coastal and delta study applies that understanding to flooding, salinity and infrastructure. Energy & Sustainability and Renewable System Design add physical and technical applications of the climate theme through generation, storage, and applied system design. The mathematics and computing sequence offers numerical differential-equation methods, linear systems, probability and data models applicable to natural systems. Sustainability Essentials I and II contain meaningful physical topics including mechanics, thermodynamics, waves and spectroscopy; the cumulative theory and laboratory sequence needed for physics is absent. General mathematical tools and basic waves are insufficient for an astronomy option covering celestial mechanics, stellar or galactic systems and observational methods. Fieldwork, spectroscopy exposure, data analysis and a partner project develop empirical skills without providing a cumulative experimental physics or instrumentation pathway. None of these three directions supports a coherent second option. There is no pair to test for distinctness. Optional UCR independent research is outside the degree and does not stand in for Utrecht’s required specialist project.
